questions.question: In 1962, who published 'The History of Ocean Basins', which outlined the theory of how tectonic plates could move, later called 'sea floor spreading'?
questions.solution: Harry Hammond Hess, an American geologist and naval officer, published The History of Ocean Basins in 1962, outlining the theory of seafloor spreading. He discovered mid-ocean ridges rising 1.5 km above the abyssal plain. Seafloor spreading is the process where tectonic plates split apart from each other.

questions.question:
Which of the following is the correct match between column-A and column-B?
Column A (Elements in earth crust)Column B (Total % in earth crust)
i. Oxygena. 8%
ii. Siliconb. 28%
iii. Aluminiumc. 47%
iv. Irond. 5%
questions.solution:
Correct matching: i-c, ii-b, iii-a, iv-d
  • Oxygen – 47% (c)
  • Silicon – 28% (b)
  • Aluminium – 8% (a)
  • Iron – 5% (d)
Other elements: Calcium (3.63%), Sodium (2.83%), Potassium (2.59%), Magnesium (2.09%). Earth has three layers: crust, mantle, core.

questions.question: Continental Shelf which is the shallowest part of the ocean has an average gradient of:
questions.solution: The Continental Shelf has an average gradient of 1° or even less. It is the extended margin of each continent occupied by relatively shallow seas and gulfs. The shelf ends at a steep slope called the shelf break. Average width is about 80 km, but can be narrower or absent in some regions (e.g., Chile, west coast of Sumatra).

questions.question: Living organisms have been on Earth for how much percent of Earth's history?
questions.solution: Living organisms have been on Earth for approximately 80% of Earth's history. Earth's age is about 4.6 billion years, and unicellular life appeared nearly 3.8 billion years ago. Calculation: 3.8/4.6 × 100 = 82.6% (approximately 80%).

questions.question:
Choose the correct statement(s) related to 'continentality'.
A. The sea exerts a moderating influence on climate.
B. As the distance from the sea increases, the people experience extreme weather conditions.
C. As one goes from the surface of the earth to higher altitudes, the atmosphere becomes less dense and temperature decreases.
questions.solution:
A and B are correct.
  • Continentality – very hot summers and very cold winters in inland areas, common between 40° and 70° north latitude.
  • A: Sea exerts moderating influence on climate – correct.
  • B: Greater distance from sea leads to extreme weather conditions – correct.
  • C: About altitude and temperature – true but not directly related to continentality.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements about oceanic trenches:
1. The Mariana Trench in the Pacific Ocean is the deepest point on Earth, with a depth of about 11,022 metres.
2. The Java Trench, located in the Indian Ocean, is deeper than the Tonga Trench in the Southwestern Pacific Ocean.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.solution:
Only Statement 1 is correct.
  • Mariana Trench (Pacific) – deepest point on Earth, about 11,022 metres – correct.
  • Java Trench (Sunda Trench, Indian Ocean) – max depth ~7,725 metres.
  • Tonga Trench (Pacific) – deepest point (Horizon Deep) ~10,882 metres, which is deeper than Java Trench.
Other trenches: Puerto Rico Trench (8,400 m) – Atlantic; South Sandwich Trench (7,432 m) – Southern Ocean.

questions.question: What does El Niño refer to?
questions.solution:
El Niño (Spanish for "Little Boy") refers to a hot water current – warming of ocean surface or above-average sea surface temperatures in the central and eastern tropical Pacific Ocean off the coast of Peru. It leads to weakening of trade winds.

La Niña ("Little Girl") is the periodic cooling of ocean surface temperatures in the same region.

questions.question: Which of the following oceans is surrounded by the continent of North America and South America to the east?
questions.solution:
The Pacific Ocean has North and South America to its east. It is the world's largest and deepest ocean, representing 45% of the global ocean surface. The International Date Line passes through it.

  • Atlantic Ocean – surrounded by North/South America to the west, Europe/Africa to the east
  • Indian Ocean – bordered by Asia (north), Africa (west), Australia (east)

questions.question:
Consider the following statements:
1. Due to the attraction of the Sun and the Moon, ocean water generally experiences two high tides and two low tides in a day.
2. Diurnal tides occur when there are two high tides and two low tides each day.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.solution:
Only Statement 1 is correct.
  • Due to Sun and Moon's attraction, ocean water generally experiences two high tides and two low tides daily – correct (semi-diurnal pattern).
  • Diurnal tides – one high tide and one low tide each day (Statement 2 is incorrect).
Tide types:
  • Semi-diurnal – two high and two low tides each day
  • Diurnal – one high and one low tide each day
  • Mixed – two highs and two lows of different heights
  • Spring tides – Sun, Earth, Moon aligned
  • Neap tides – Sun at right angle to Moon

questions.question: Which of the following oceans extends into the Mediterranean Sea?
questions.solution: The Atlantic Ocean is the second largest ocean in the world. The Mediterranean Sea is an intercontinental sea located between Europe, North Africa, and Western Asia. It is connected to the Atlantic Ocean specifically through the Strait of Gibraltar.

questions.question: The mohororvicic (Moho) discontinuity separates?
questions.option_3: Earth's crust and the inner core
questions.solution: The Moho discontinuity separates the Earth's crust from the mantle. It is found at an average depth of about 8 km beneath ocean basins and approximately 32 km beneath continental surfaces.

questions.question: Which is the correct sequence of oceans according to size (from largest to smallest)?
questions.option_1: Pacific Ocean > Antarctic Ocean > Indian Ocean > Atlantic Ocean
questions.option_2: Pacific Ocean > Indian Ocean > Antarctic Ocean > Atlantic Ocean
questions.option_3: Pacific Ocean > Atlantic Ocean > Indian Ocean > Antarctic Ocean
questions.option_4: Pacific Ocean > Indian Ocean > Atlantic Ocean > Antarctic Ocean
questions.solution: The correct order of oceans by size from largest to smallest is: Pacific Ocean, Atlantic Ocean, Indian Ocean, and Antarctic (Southern) Ocean. The Pacific Ocean is the world's largest and was named by Ferdinand Magellan.

questions.question: The percentage of earth's water found in the oceans is _________.
questions.solution:
Approximately 97.2% of Earth's water is found in the oceans. The remaining water is distributed as follows:
  • Glaciers: 2.1%
  • Groundwater: 0.61%
  • Freshwater lakes: 0.009%
Only about 2.7% of all Earth's water is fresh water.

questions.question: How thick is the lithosphere?
questions.solution: The lithosphere ranges from 10 to 200 km in thickness. It is the outermost mechanical layer of Earth, comprising the crust and the uppermost portion of the mantle.

questions.question: The crust is the Earth's outermost layer that is less than ______ percent of Earth by mass, with oceanic crust and continental crust often consisting of more felsic rocks.
questions.solution:
The crust makes up less than 1% of Earth's total mass.
  • Continental crust: About 30 km thick, composed of lighter felsic rocks like granite.
  • Oceanic crust: About 5 km thick, composed of dense mafic rocks like basalt.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements:
1. The movement of Earth's plates is classified into three main types of tectonic boundaries.
2. Convergent, divergent, and transform are the three primary types of plate movements.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.solution:
Both statements are correct. Plate movements create three types of boundaries:
  • Convergent: Plates move toward each other.
  • Divergent: Plates move apart.
  • Transform: Plates slide sideways past each other.

questions.question: Movement of fault lines can cause:
questions.solution: The movement of fault lines causes earthquakes. These occur at plate boundaries known as fault zones. A seismograph is the instrument used to measure earthquakes.

questions.question: What is the average salinity of the Indian ocean?
questions.solution: The average salinity is 35 o/oo (35 parts per thousand). Salinity refers to the amount of salt (in grams) dissolved in 1000 grams of water.

questions.question: Tsunami is NOT caused by:
questions.solution: Hurricanes do not cause tsunamis. Tsunamis are giant waves triggered by geological displacements under the sea, such as earthquakes, volcanic eruptions, or undersea landslides.

questions.question: Which of the following is a warm current?
questions.solution:
The Gulf Stream is a warm current in the North Atlantic.
Examples of Warm Currents: Gulf Stream, Kuroshio, Brazilian, Alaskan.
Examples of Cold Currents: Labrador, Canary, Falkland, Benguela.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding oceanic landforms:
1. An Atoll is a group of islands found in tropical oceans, consisting of coral reefs and a central depression.
2. A guyot is a shallow body of water separated from the ocean by a barrier reef.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.solution: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is incorrect because a guyot is an undersea flat-topped mountain. A shallow body of water separated from the ocean by a reef is called a lagoon.

questions.question: Ocean acidification is the ongoing decrease in the pH of the Earth’s oceans, caused by the uptake of ______ from the atmosphere.
questions.solution: Ocean acidification is caused by the absorption of carbon dioxide (CO2) from the atmosphere, which reduces the pH of seawater and affects marine food chains.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding the lowest known point on Earth:
1. Challenger Deep is located in the western Pacific Ocean.
2. The Great Barrier Reef is the world’s largest coral reef located in Australia.
3. Factorian Deep is the deepest point in the Pacific Ocean.
Which of the statements given above is incorrect?
questions.solution: Statement 3 is incorrect. The Challenger Deep is the deepest point in the Pacific Ocean. Factorian Deep is actually the deepest point in the Southern Ocean (Antarctica).

questions.question: In coastal areas, during the night, wind blows from land to sea because:
questions.option_1: low pressure is created on land
questions.option_4: high pressure is created at sea
questions.solution: During the night, water cools slower than land. This maintains warmer air (low pressure) over the sea, while the cooler air (high pressure) over the land blows toward the sea, creating a land breeze.

questions.question: The process of seepage of water into the ground is called ____.
questions.solution: Infiltration is the process by which surface water enters the soil or seeps into the ground.
